question: In December 2021, the World Health Assembly agreed to launch a global process to draft and negotiate an international instrument under the Constitution of the World Health Organization to strengthen pandemic prevention, preparedness and response. In April 2024, a new and much more general proposal was published. With the last stages of the negotiations in mind: 1.
What is the Commission’s position on the latest published proposal and is the Commission planning to consult Parliament?

Can the Commission confirm that it is making pandemic prevention at source a priority in the negotiations and that this is not an issue it is willing to compromise on? Prevention at source means preventing pathogen spillovers and the emergence and re-emergence of diseases at human-animal-environment interfaces from happening in the first place.
Will the Commission make global equitable access to health technologies its priority in the final stages of negotiations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.6.2024) The Bureau of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Body (INB) released a revised draft of the negotiating text for the pandemic agreement on 22 April 20241. Several areas required further work to enable consensus and a meaningful and ratifiable pandemic agreement.

In the following rounds of negotiations, the EU carefully listened to its partners and made significant efforts in search of convergence. However, while much progress has been achieved, World Health Organisation Member States did not reach consensus by the ambitious deadline of the 77th World Health Assembly (WHA)2.

An extension of the negotiations was decided, foreseeing completion by the 78th WHA (May 2025) or earlier by way of a special session of the WHA during 2024, if possible. The EU remains committed to concluding a robust pandemic agreement as a crucial element for a stronger, more resilient, and more equitable global health architecture.

The Commission confirms that, in line with the negotiating directives as annexed to Council Decision (EU) 2022/4513, it will continue in the extended negotiations to prioritise equity considerations, including for the access to countermeasures and effective prevention, including through the One Health approach.
In line with Article 218(10) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the Commission will continue to inform the European Parliament on the state of play of the negotiations.
